verdict.rationale: Nix's own manual says it can automatically skip building from source and download pre-built binaries from a binary cache, and nix.dev lists transparent binary caching as a core feature. A community report of building once on remote builders and sharing results across devs and CI corroborates this in practice. Missing for 10: in-depth documentation of configuring caches/substituters (e.g. trust keys, custom caches), and hands-on evidence of the default public cache serving common packages.

support.subject: As a developer, I can install prebuilt binary packages from a cache instead of compiling from source

citations.quote: Nix can automatically skip building from source and instead use a binary cache, a web server that provides pre-built binaries.
Transparent build caching using binary caches
the command `nix-shell` will build or download those dependencies if they’re not already in your Nix store
Everything is only built once, on a large set of specialized remote builders, then shared among all of our devs, CI, and deployment infrastructure.
